findings.conditions: two hypre_LocateAssumedPartition calls on the same comm back to back with no intervening synchronising exchange; a fast rank enters the second call while a slow rank still waits in the first; slow rank's locate rows come from >=2 owners
findings.reasoning: The receive loop takes hypre_MPI_ANY_SOURCE with the fixed tag flag1=17 and stops only when rows_found == locate_row_count. The function has no barrier, and the Isends complete eagerly, so a rank that has collected its own rows can start the next call and send another tag-17 range to a rank still inside the previous call. That receive can take the new message in place of an outstanding one from another owner. proc_list/row ranges are then wrong (one owner listed twice, another missing), or rows_found overshoots and the != loop never ends (hang). The stale message is then consumed by the next call, which corrupts its partition too and gives a wrong comm package.

findings.conditions: updatefaceElemMatrix: any other point-to-point message on mpiComm_ in flight (from a rank that has already returned and continued, or later FEI traffic) when the owner posts its wildcard receive
findings.reasoning: The owner receives with MPI_ANY_SOURCE and MPI_ANY_TAG, then treats Status.MPI_TAG as a face global ID: k = BinarySearch(tag, faceList, nFaces), with no check for k<0. The Isends (tag = face ID) are never waited on, and nothing synchronises after the receives, so a rank that leaves early can send later messages (e.g. tags 33420/33421 or other face-tagged traffic) that this receive matches. With a foreign tag, k=-1 and cols[-1]/ncols[-1] are indexed (crash). A message from a different face also merges the wrong columns into the face element matrix (wrong result). Which message wins depends on arrival order.

findings.conditions: MPI implementation does not buffer the 1-int MPI_Send (synchronous/rendezvous mode, eager limit 0) and the send graph has a cycle (symmetric neighbours)
findings.reasoning: Every rank first does blocking MPI_Send of its lengths (tag 539) to all recvProc, and only then posts MPI_Recv(MPI_ANY_SOURCE, 539). No receive is pre-posted, so with unbuffered sends two neighbours that send to each other both block in MPI_Send: a buffering-dependent deadlock. The same code is in HYPRE_LSI_mlmaxwell.c:943. The ANY_SOURCE receive also sets sendProc[i] from whichever sender arrives first; that is consistent, but the order of sendProc differs between runs.

findings.conditions: unbuffered MPI_Send of the nlevels-int rnum array; ranks are mutual neighbours
findings.reasoning: In hypre_SetUpFactor each rank does blocking hypre_MPI_Send(rnum, nlevels, ..., TAG_SetUp_rnum) to all spes before any receive is posted, then hypre_MPI_Recv from each rpes. If the send is not buffered (large nlevels above the eager limit, or synchronous mode), mutually communicating ranks block in Send waiting for each other. Completion relies on MPI buffering.

findings.conditions: ExchangePrunedRows/Ext multi-level loop: a fast rank reaches level k+1 and sends a ROW_PRUNED_REQ_TAG request while the target is still in its level-k receive loop
findings.reasoning: ReceiveRequest probes hypre_MPI_ANY_SOURCE with the same tag at every level. The only synchronisation between levels is an Allreduce of per-level counts, and requests are sent before it. So a level-(k+1) request can be counted as a level-k one, and a stale level-k request is then served at level k+1. Replies come from the server's static local pruned rows, so the swap is mostly harmless, but per-level counts and reply bookkeeping (mem freed per level, requests per level) depend on the interleaving. Any server-side state that changes per level would make the result wrong.
